title: Apple GPU RMSNorm SIMD-group reduction comparison
question: Does one hybrid SIMD-group reduction materially reduce synchronized Apple GPU RMSNorm dispatch latency versus the shared-memory tree without a relevant workload regression?
hypothesis: Replacing the 128-value shared-memory tree with four 32-lane SIMD-group reductions and one cross-group reduction will reduce shared storage and workgroup barriers enough to improve at least one real Qwen decode or prefill regime by 5% or more.

variant.local_accumulation: Each thread accumulates the same strided BF16 values into FP32 as the baseline.
variant.within_group_reduction: Four 32-lane SIMD groups reduce their FP32 thread sums with warp.sum.
variant.cross_group_reduction: Four group leaders write FP32 partials to shared memory; the first SIMD group reduces those four values.
variant.scope_boundary: One explicit kernel and enqueue entrypoint. No general reduction abstraction or runtime dispatch framework.

correctness.authority: tests/test_rms_norm.mojo and the existing committed Transformers oracle fixtures
correctness.command: MODULAR_DEBUG=device-sync-mode uv run --locked mojo run -I src -I tests tests/test_rms_norm.mojo
correctness.gate: Both baseline and variant must produce finite outputs within the frozen tolerance before performance collection.

workloads.semantic_role: V0 context-boundary prefill-like; EXP-0001 largest measured

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_rms_norm.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0002 --run-id EXP-0002-RUN-001 --variant-comparison --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0002-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.timing_boundary: The same GPU-aware bencher completion boundary used by EXP-0001; allocation, initialization, correctness checks, compilation, and host mapping remain excluded.
block_order: ascending rows; baseline then variant per workload
descending rows; variant then baseline per workload
descending rows; variant then baseline per workload
ascending rows; baseline then variant per workload
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: For each block and workload, divide the variant median by the baseline median. Summarize the four paired ratios with their median and retain every block ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC Power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal identity, stable display configuration, and no deliberate competing workload.

decision_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and variant faster in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and variant slower in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.replace_baseline: At least one relevant workload meets material_improvement and no relevant workload meets material_regression.
decision_rule.retain_baseline: No relevant workload meets material_improvement, or a relevant regression outweighs a regime-specific benefit without a justified caller-level dispatch decision.
decision_rule.inconclusive_band: Effects between -5% and +5% are not optimization wins even if their point estimate favors the variant.
decision_rule.crossover: A dispatch rule is outside the default scope. Consider one explicit row threshold only if opposite effects both exceed 5%, repeat in at least three blocks, and map to real V0 callers.

generated_code_check.purpose: Confirm the variant lowers to the intended structure, not establish performance causality.
expected: SIMD-group reduction operations appear in the Metal sidecar.
Shared reduction storage falls from 128 FP32 values to four.
Workgroup barriers fall from nine to two.

profiling_rule: Profile the variant only after ordinary paired timing shows a material effect. Use short captures and retain unavailable counters as unresolved.

profiling_result.bounded_finding: Both xctrace attempts held the target before its first instruction. The auditable retry ended with SIGKILL and zero Metal command-buffer submissions, while the same short binary completed normally outside Instruments.
profiling_result.decision_effect: No mechanism claim is available; the failed traces do not invalidate ordinary timing or clean generated-code structure.

completion_conditions: The variant passes the frozen numerical correctness cases.
Generated code is consistent with the declared structural variant.
All four paired blocks pass environment, device, parse, and sample-count gates.
Each implementation and workload has 40 valid samples and four retained paired block ratios.
The decision follows the predeclared 5% and direction-consistency rules.
The production implementation, experiment report, and nonclaims agree.
stop_conditions: The variant does not lower to the intended SIMD-group structure.
AC power, thermal, cleanliness, device identity, or parsing gates fail.
Either implementation loses a declared repetition or iteration count.
nonclaims: No end-to-end inference, model-phase, time-to-first-token, or time-per-output-token result.
No causal attribution from timing alone.
No observed hardware bandwidth or occupancy claim without a named counter.
No general claim that SIMD-group reduction is optimal for other hidden sizes or GPUs.

deviations.from_protocol: A valid short rows=512 Metal System Trace was attempted after the material timing effect.
deviations.observed: Instruments held both launched targets before execution; no valid trace sequence was collected.
deviations.treatment: Exclude both captures, retain the profiler limitation, and make no trace-derived mechanism claim.

decision.production_action: Use the SIMD-group kernel as the single public Apple GPU RMSNorm default; retain the shared tree only as an explicit benchmark baseline.
decision.reason: One relevant workload materially improved, no relevant workload materially regressed, and no opposite effects met the frozen crossover rule.
